tags.gist: The society backs a regulatory approach protecting patients while allowing timely access to safe, effective innovation.
Recommends FDA mandate that action-directing or action-taking functions with moderate or severe consequences join an independently governed, qualified postmarket data system.
Recommends formally studying non-directive informational tools and exempt non-device CDS through similar data systems to learn their risks and benefits.
Says joining a qualified data system with expert review should be necessary but not sufficient for accepting premarket uncertainty; some cases still need trials.
Says its recommendations, built on existing specialty programs, would connect GenAI use with downstream actions and outcomes and build trust.

Lists seven recommendations: required data-system participation, qualification criteria, manufacturer accountability, links to change control, shared benchmarking, bidirectional escalation and FDA-CMS coordination.
Supports the lifecycle approach but says greater postmarket reliance is justified only with operational monitoring infrastructure overseen by expert clinicians.
Cites a review of device reports for 823 AI devices, almost all concerning five devices, showing the limits of passive reporting.
Says manufacturer inference records and institutional outcomes must be linked to assess use, overrides and subgroup performance, supporting all three approaches.
Says the clinician analogy justifies ongoing assessment akin to maintenance of certification, without implying licensure or replacing authorization.
Points to precedent for society-administered postmarket data programs and urges connecting with existing ones rather than duplicating them.
Describes coverage-linked national data programs for valve replacement and appendage closure, and a vascular network linked to claims.
Describes an FDA-sponsored orthopedic data collaboration and radiology's imaging AI monitoring program as relevant, linkable infrastructure.
Draws lessons of independent governance, meaningful data and durable participation enabled by CMS.
Says unregulated CDS often fails to match claims and the non-device CDS four-point test seems arbitrary now that chatbots analyze images and signals.
Recommends mandatory qualified data-system participation for action-directing, action-taking or moderate-to-severe-consequence functions.
Recommends studying unregulated non-device CDS and non-directive tools through similar data systems.
Asks FDA to identify the legal mechanism per category, such as section 522 orders or special controls, and engage legislators where authority is lacking.
Wants the data system's core functions operational at launch; a promise to monitor later should not reduce premarket evidence.
Says participation alone cannot justify uncertainty; for irreversible high-consequence functions, monitoring must not replace premarket evidence including trials.
Wants surveillance duration tied to ongoing change in models and prompts, not to a payer's evidence timeline or regulatory deadline.
Wants qualified data systems governed with professional societies, independent of manufacturers and developers, with industry holding no control over adjudication.
Wants the system to capture every encounter with a full denominator, version identity at inference, links from outputs to actions and outcomes, and subgroup results.
Wants scheduled independent audits, qualified reviewers, transparent version-specific reporting, privacy-limited collection and guaranteed FDA access and continuity.
Keeps roles distinct: the system measures, FDA oversees, manufacturers remain responsible for reporting and corrective action, with independent escalation.
Wants sustainable independent funding without buying favorable findings, transparent conflicts, and multiple qualified operators rather than an exclusive one.
Supports all three approaches, with re-benchmarking on stable plus contemporary cases and clinician review of prespecified samples by independent, qualified reviewers.
Wants degradation monitoring against the baseline with routine cadence, event triggers and prespecified thresholds prompting investigation, rollback or suspension.
Treats a prespecified performance envelope as a monitoring component, not a substitute for defining permissible change, since averages hide subgroup deterioration.
Wants contractual notification combined with version identifiers, pinning, logs and rollback, acknowledging data systems may miss hidden revisions.
Wants supervisory agents independently evaluated against clinician adjudication and outcomes, logged in the data system, and supplementing not displacing clinical review.
Says a society-involved data system can supply a multi-institutional sampling frame and sequestered, versioned, refreshed test sets, plus qualified adjudicators.
Says sponsors must still show the benchmark measures relevant capabilities and relates to clinical performance; a distributed system is not presumed representative.
Supports qualified third-party roles informed by ASCA and MDDT, with societies eligible when qualified, but affiliation conferring neither qualification nor approval authority.
Agrees both escalation errors matter; wants prespecified criteria from independent society-chosen experts, linked outcomes, and separate rates not averaged.
Recommends FDA-CMS coordination on data elements and qualification, with payment policy complementing rather than sustaining surveillance alone.
Concludes qualified independent data systems linking AI use to outcomes should be required for the identified functions.
States the principle that more postmarket reliance requires a matching credible ability to produce and act on evidence, societies contributing without assuming responsibility.
Measure under- and over-escalation separately with prespecified criteria, a complete denominator and linked outcomes, keeping event reporting.
Use sequestered, versioned, refreshed test sets from the data system with documented sampling and adjudication; data source alone does not establish validity.
Make societies and data-program operators eligible third parties under transparent criteria, avoiding exclusive operators or automatic qualification.
A qualified data system that is operational is necessary but not sufficient for reduced premarket evidence; irreversible risks may need stronger confirmation.
Combine re-benchmarking, independent clinician review and degradation monitoring with a defined denominator, prespecified cadence, triggers and thresholds.
Independently evaluate supervisory agents, keep auditable records, assess missed and correlated failures and keep human oversight; model agreement alone is insufficient.
Societies measure and report independently, manufacturers keep regulatory obligations, institutions keep theirs, with FDA access and FDA-CMS coordination.
Scale post-change evaluation to the modification's nature and risk including safety-critical tasks and subgroups; data-system measures supplement validation.
Treat a prespecified performance envelope only as a monitoring tool, not authorization for unspecified changes, within PCCP boundaries.
Combine contractual notification with version identity, configuration records, testing and rollback; data-system signals aid investigation but guarantee no detection.
